outcome: side effects (skin changes, mood changes, arm pain, numbness)
cohort: The study included 345 women who underwent etonogestrel subdermal implant insertion at King Abdulaziz Medical City in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between 2019 and 2022.
finding: The study found that 88% of women using etonogestrel subdermal implants experienced menstrual abnormalities, with a discontinuation rate of 22% before 36 months of use, primarily due to these and other side effects.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from electronic medical records of ESI insertions between 2019 and 2022, supplemented by phone-based questionnaires to assess outcomes up to 36 months post-insertion.
